Spectacled with Baïkal

Server compatibility 9 September 2026

Baïkal is a small, self-hosted CalDAV and CardDAV server written in PHP and built on the sabre/dav library. It stores its data in SQLite or MySQL, runs happily on shared hosting, a NAS or a Raspberry Pi, and comes with a minimal web admin for managing users and collections. If you want your own CalDAV server without running a full groupware suite, Baïkal is one of the smallest ways to get there.

Compatibility at a glance

AppStatusNotes
Spectacled Journals✅ WorksNo issues found
Spectacled Notes✅ WorksNo issues found
Spectacled Tasks✅ WorksNo issues found

We tested all three apps against a Baïkal instance: account setup and discovery, creating and deleting collections, and creating, editing, moving and deleting entries. Everything behaved as expected — no sync errors, no lost data, no server-side quirks to work around.

One thing to check first

Spectacled authenticates with HTTP Basic only. Baïkal can be configured for either Digest or Basic authentication, and if it is set to Digest, the apps cannot log in — you will just get a failed login with correct credentials. Switch your Baïkal instance to Basic before adding the account.

Switching Baïkal from Digest to Basic

The authentication type is a Baïkal setting, not a per-user one. Open the Baïkal admin web interface, go to Settings, and set the WebDAV authentication type to Basic. (On older installations the same option lives in Baïkal's configuration file rather than the admin UI.) Existing accounts and passwords keep working; only the way clients prove them changes.

Use HTTPS

Basic authentication sends your username and password Base64-encoded, which is encoding, not encryption — anyone who can read the traffic can read the credentials. Digest was designed to avoid exactly that on plain HTTP. So if you switch to Basic, serve Baïkal over HTTPS. With TLS in front, Basic is the standard way CalDAV clients authenticate, and it is what most other clients use too.

If you administer the server yourself, this is a one-minute change. If you are on hosting where you cannot change the setting, Spectacled will not be able to connect for now — Digest support is not implemented in the apps.

Connecting an account

In the app, add an account and enter your Baïkal CalDAV URL together with your Baïkal username and password. The URL is usually the dav.php endpoint, for example https://dav.example.com/dav.php/; Baïkal shows the exact address for each user in its admin interface. Spectacled also retries via /.well-known/caldav, so the bare host name works as well if your web server has Baïkal's well-known redirect in place.

After login, Spectacled lists the collections it can actually use. Journals and Notes store their entries as VJOURNAL, Tasks uses VTODO, so a collection only shows up if it supports one of those components — a calendar created for events only will not appear. You can also let Spectacled create a new collection for you during setup, which is the quickest route: it requests the right component set itself.

If you use the web app

The browser build is a special case, and it is not Baïkal's fault: browsers enforce CORS, and CalDAV servers generally do not send the headers a browser needs for cross-origin WebDAV requests. The web app therefore talks to your server through a small CORS proxy, which you should self-host — it terminates TLS and would otherwise let a third party see your credentials. The Android, iOS and desktop apps contact Baïkal directly and need none of this.

Verdict

Baïkal is a good match for Spectacled: light to run, standards-compliant, and it worked with all three apps without a single workaround. Set the authentication type to Basic, put it behind HTTPS, and you are done.

Found something that does not match your experience, or tested Spectacled against another server? Please open an issue — server reports are how this section grows.
